headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0075 — SMTO couldn't process the clipboard image

html:
SMTO-EXE-0075 — SMTO couldn't process the clipboard image

GUID: 20a26c5b-3c45-5a5b-8915-650371f32f1c
Slug: clipboard-image-codec
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: clipboard

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't read or prepare the image for the Gateway computer's clipboard. Either image support isn't installed there, or the image isn't a normal PNG, JPEG, BMP or TIFF picture. The clipboard wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Use a PNG, JPEG, BMP or TIFF image and check that it opens normally in an image viewer on the Gateway computer. SMTO only accepts these standard picture types and refuses damaged or unusual image files.
  2. If you copied the image from an app, save it as a PNG file first, then copy or use that saved file. Some apps put pictures on the clipboard in forms SMTO can't read, while a saved PNG always works.
  3. If no image works at all, ask the person who manages the Gateway to install its image support (Pillow), restart it, and then start a new task. Without that component the Gateway can't handle any clipboard images.

What success looks like

  • SMTO copies or reads the image and reports its size in pixels.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the image type you used, to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't send private images with the report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Clipboard image normalization failed: Pillow could not be imported on the Gateway, or the bytes could not be decoded as an allowed PNG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF or DIB image.

What this means

  • The image normalization path could not import Pillow or decode/convert the supplied bytes as one of its supported bounded inert raster formats. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • The image normalization path could not import Pillow or decode/convert the supplied bytes as one of its supported bounded inert raster formats.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish a missing codec from invalid/unsupported image bytes and inspect the source format without treating its filename as proof.

How to fix it

  • Install Pillow in the Gateway's Python environment and use a valid PNG, JPEG, BMP or TIFF image within 16 MiB and 16 million pixels (image_png in src/gateway_core/platform_clipboard/protocol.py). Restart the Gateway and refresh its capabilities after installing Pillow.
  • Install Pillow on the Gateway and use a valid bounded PNG, JPEG, BMP or TIFF image.

Retry and execution caution

  • Install Pillow on the Gateway and use a valid bounded PNG, JPEG, BMP or TIFF image.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported valid raster normalizes to bounded RGB/RGBA PNG before any write.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain clipboard write or include content in diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
